source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 217: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: the hang is reproducible during process-group/NCCL initialization, the launcher can collect per-rank logs, and no platform, driver, or network detail is known until measured. Treat timings, topology, and capacity claims as measured facts only after collection.

Hypothesis: one or more ranks disagree about world size/rank assignment, rendezvous identity, collective ordering, or the selected interface/address, preventing a common membership from forming. A competing hypothesis is a topology, GPU-visibility, container, resource, or transport-path fault. Falsification requires every rank to report the same job/attempt ID, world size, rank/local rank, device UUID, rendezvous endpoint, interface/path, and collective sequence, and requires a successful checksum-verified minimal all-reduce under the same configuration.

1. First preserve a timestamped, redacted baseline: launcher configuration, rank map, host and container identity, CUDA-visible devices and UUIDs, GPU count/topology, driver/runtime/library versions, CPU/memory/FD/SHM limits, rendezvous/store endpoint and resolved addresses, selected interfaces, and per-rank logs. Confirm authorization; redact credentials, tokens, private addresses, and unrelated tenant data.
2. Verify that each expected rank joined exactly once, that rank/world-size/local-rank values and rendezvous job ID match, and that all ranks reach collectives in the same order. Check stale stores, duplicate jobs, address resolution, firewall/port reachability, interface selection, and timeout settings without changing multiple variables at once. Confirm GPU visibility, device exclusivity, peer access/topology, container device permissions, shared memory, file descriptors, and host resource headroom.
3. Run a bounded, isolated minimal all-reduce with a watchdog and explicit cleanup, recording start/end timestamps, phase of failure, rank-specific errors, checksum correctness, success/timeout/failure counts, and latency distributions. Use repeated matched trials (predeclared count and seed) for single-node, reduced-world, and full-world configurations. Hold software, message size, rank placement, and launch parameters constant; vary only one suspected interface/path or world-size factor per comparison. Never infer causality from one timeout.

Interpretation: a deterministic rank/rendezvous mismatch or missing rank supports the membership hypothesis; success in single-node but failure in reduced/full world supports an inter-host interface, route, firewall, or transport hypothesis; failures tied to a device or placement support GPU/topology/container/resource causes. Record confounders such as load, retries, warm-up, caching, clock skew, concurrent jobs, and changed network paths. A timeout is evidence of an unsuccessful trial, not proof of a specific cause.

Safety and rollback: use a disposable diagnostic job, bounded timeouts, rate-limited retries, and a kill/cleanup watchdog. Do not alter production traffic or persistent rendezvous state without authorization. Revert any diagnostic environment/interface override after each trial, retain before/after configuration, stop if error rates or resource pressure rise, and escalate with the redacted evidence bundle. Proceed to remediation only when repeated evidence identifies a cause and a reversible change has a defined success and rollback gate.
risks: A timeout cannot by itself distinguish rendezvous, collective-order, topology, resource, or transport failure.
Changing interface, timeout, rank placement, retries, or rendezvous state can confound comparisons or worsen an unhealthy job.
Per-rank logs and network manifests may contain credentials, private addresses, or sensitive infrastructure details.
evidence_required: Redacted per-rank environment and rank/world-size/rendezvous records; topology, GPU visibility, container/resource, interface and path evidence; repeated matched single-node, reduced-world, and full-world minimal all-reduce results with checksums and latency distributions; phase-specific timeout, failure, and cleanup logs.

Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: the hang is reproducible during process-group/NCCL initialization, the launcher can collect per-rank logs, and no platform, driver, or network detail is known until measured. Treat timings, topology, and capacity claims as measured facts only after collection.

Hypothesis: one or more ranks disagree about world size/rank assignment, rendezvous identity, collective ordering, or the selected interface/address, preventing a common membership from forming. A competing hypothesis is a topology, GPU-visibility, container, resource, or transport-path fault. Falsification requires every rank to report the same job/attempt ID, world size, rank/local rank, device UUID, rendezvous endpoint, interface/path, and collective sequence, and requires a successful checksum-verified minimal all-reduce under the same configuration.

1. First preserve a timestamped, redacted baseline: launcher configuration, rank map, host and container identity, CUDA-visible devices and UUIDs, GPU count/topology, driver/runtime/library versions, CPU/memory/FD/SHM limits, rendezvous/store endpoint and resolved addresses, selected interfaces, and per-rank logs. Confirm authorization; redact credentials, tokens, private addresses, and unrelated tenant data.
2. Verify that each expected rank joined exactly once, that rank/world-size/local-rank values and rendezvous job ID match, and that all ranks reach collectives in the same order. Check stale stores, duplicate jobs, address resolution, firewall/port reachability, interface selection, and timeout settings without changing multiple variables at once. Confirm GPU visibility, device exclusivity, peer access/topology, container device permissions, shared memory, file descriptors, and host resource headroom.
3. Run a bounded, isolated minimal all-reduce with a watchdog and explicit cleanup, recording start/end timestamps, phase of failure, rank-specific errors, checksum correctness, success/timeout/failure counts, and latency distributions. Use repeated matched trials (predeclared count and seed) for single-node, reduced-world, and full-world configurations. Hold software, message size, rank placement, and launch parameters constant; vary only one suspected interface/path or world-size factor per comparison. Never infer causality from one timeout.

Interpretation: a deterministic rank/rendezvous mismatch or missing rank supports the membership hypothesis; success in single-node but failure in reduced/full world supports an inter-host interface, route, firewall, or transport hypothesis; failures tied to a device or placement support GPU/topology/container/resource causes. Record confounders such as load, retries, warm-up, caching, clock skew, concurrent jobs, and changed network paths. A timeout is evidence of an unsuccessful trial, not proof of a specific cause.

Safety and rollback: use a disposable diagnostic job, bounded timeouts, rate-limited retries, and a kill/cleanup watchdog. Do not alter production traffic or persistent rendezvous state without authorization. Revert any diagnostic environment/interface override after each trial, retain before/after configuration, stop if error rates or resource pressure rise, and escalate with the redacted evidence bundle. Proceed to remediation only when repeated evidence identifies a cause and a reversible change has a defined success and rollback gate.
risks: A timeout cannot by itself distinguish rendezvous, collective-order, topology, resource, or transport failure.
Changing interface, timeout, rank placement, retries, or rendezvous state can confound comparisons or worsen an unhealthy job.
Per-rank logs and network manifests may contain credentials, private addresses, or sensitive infrastructure details.
evidence_required: Redacted per-rank environment and rank/world-size/rendezvous records; topology, GPU visibility, container/resource, interface and path evidence; repeated matched single-node, reduced-world, and full-world minimal all-reduce results with checksums and latency distributions; phase-specific timeout, failure, and cleanup logs.
